practicality.justification: The recommendation is actionable for a small operator: it gives a clear offer, display locations, a 50/50 split with control, a full 30-day run, and a concrete profit-per-visitor metric. It is somewhat demanding because it requires visitor-level randomization, persistent assignment, and a contribution-margin calculation that includes several variable costs, but the plan is usable.
quotes: Primary metric: contribution profit per visitor.
Keep visitors in the same group on repeat visits.
practicality.improvement: Add a minimum detectable effect or sample-size/power estimate, and provide a simpler starter metric for operators who cannot calculate payment fees, fulfillment costs, and return reserves at visitor level from day one.

specificity.justification: The answer uses the supplied AOV, margin, and shipping cost to propose an exact offer and threshold, shows the margin arithmetic, defines the primary metric with a formula, and gives a profit-based decision rule rather than a revenue-based one.
quotes: Test free shipping on orders of $95 or more first.
Contribution profit = merchandise revenue after discounts + shipping fees collected − product cost − actual shipping expense − payment fees − variable fulfillment costs − return/refund costs
Keep the offer only if contribution profit per visitor rises—not merely revenue or conversion.
specificity.improvement: State an explicit numeric decision threshold for the profit-per-visitor lift, such as a 90% confidence interval entirely above $0.00 or a minimum lift of $0.10 per visitor, so the final go/no-go is less subjective.

risk_awareness.justification: The response identifies the main margin and customer-behavior risks, including existing high-AOV customers capturing free shipping, buyers who would have purchased anyway, add-on products not having the average margin, and returns maturing after day 30. It also controls experiment-design risks by holding other variables constant and warning against early stopping.
quotes: Customers already ordering above $95 may simply stop paying shipping, and customers who would have bought anyway may receive the benefit without adding items.
Use actual item margins and shipping costs where possible; add-on products may not have your average 42% margin.
Run for the full 30 days rather than stopping when early results look favorable.
risk_awareness.improvement: Add a control for existing high-AOV customers, such as reporting the qualifying-order rate and shipping subsidy separately for that segment, and set a maximum shipping-cost exposure or prepaid-return cap before launch.

overall_impression: A strong, margin-aware recommendation that correctly prioritizes a shipping-threshold offer over a sitewide discount and provides a practical experiment plan with appropriate profit-based measurement and risk controls.
